overview: White starts 1.h3 and follows with the waiting 2.a3, a very slow set-up without a clear plan. Black can occupy the centre freely with ...d5, ...Nf6 and ...Bd6, and White tries to catch up with e4 or g3-Bg2 later. There is no forcing theory, and the line is chosen almost entirely for surprise.

white_ideas.idea: Make useful waiting moves and develop later with Nf3 and g3
Fight for the centre with e4 once Black commits
Avoid theory and play a quiet game

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...d5, ...Nf6 and ...Bc5 or ...Bd6
Develop freely and use the extra tempi
Punish the slow start with a space advantage

typical_structures.structure: Black classical centre with White flank pawns on a3/h3
Reversed set-ups depending on White's later e4/d4

character.notes: Slow, quiet play with no early pressure on either side.

soundness.notes: Not refuted, but gives Black an easy game; I treat it as sound with low confidence.

structure.notes: The centre is undecided and Black can build it first.

approach.notes: Strong players essentially never play it.

level.notes: Neither memory nor understanding is demanding; it is simply a low-quality set-up for White.

character.reason: Quiet but without a hard-to-break structure.

level.reason: Not a good first choice, but not hard.
